task: Close the three MUST violations of the SKIP-clause rule in .agents/governance/skill-description-trigger-standard.md, where a skill sharing a naming family with a sibling carries no negative trigger routing away from it.

events.content: Measured the SKIP-clause rule mechanically instead of reading descriptions by hand. Parsed the frontmatter description of all 96 skills under .claude/skills, grouped them into naming families by leading token, and flagged every family member whose description carries no negative trigger.
Found 8 families with more than one member, covering 37 of the 96 skills, and exactly 3 members with no SKIP clause: github, session-end, session-log-fixer.

Falsified a wider claim from an earlier pass. A looser heuristic had flagged autoplan, benchmark-models, steering-matcher, and stuck-detection for naming no real skill. Reading the actual clauses shows none of the four sits in a multi-member family, so the family-scoped rule does not bind them, and panning-for-gold's referents both resolve: analyst is an agent and spec-generator is a skill. Scope reduced from 7 edits to 3.

Wrote reciprocal clauses. github now routes URL reading to github-url-intercept, which already routed PR and comment work back to github. session-log-fixer routes local completion to session-end, and session-end routes creation to session-init and CI repair to session-log-fixer. session-init already routes to the session parent, which satisfies the chaining-parent escape in the standard.
Regenerated the copilot-cli skill mirrors with build_all.py so the generated tree matches the canonical tree, and bumped both parity plugin manifests to 0.6.137.
Re-ran the measurement after the edits: 0 family members without a SKIP clause. Verified each edited description stays under 1024 chars, carries no angle brackets, and carries no en or em dash.
